title: Unit Economics Dashboard – API Contract Sketch (v0)
content:
Context
- This is a rough contract sketch for Console backend endpoints powering the internal “Unit Economics” dashboard.
- Intended consumers: Console UI (internal-only), Finance ad-hoc analysis (read-only), and automated checks (data quality / reconciliation view).
- Not final. Expect iteration once aggregation tables + dimension mapping stabilize.

Primary metric
- blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens (a.k.a. “blended $/1M output tokens”)
- Output tokens is the denominator (NOT total tokens); must be streaming-parity.
- This API should return enough supporting numbers to explain changes: total_cost_usd, output_tokens, requests, cache_hit_rate, batching_efficiency.

Goals (API)
- Single flexible query model for:
  1) time series (chart)
  2) breakdown tables (group_by one or more dims)
  3) top-N (ranked tables)
- Strong input validation: dimension allowlist, cardinality guardrails, forbidden customer-identifying drilldowns.
- Cursor-based pagination for large breakdowns.
- Ability to request “live view” vs “finance view” (different caching + freshness semantics).

Non-goals (v0)
- Exposing customer_id, request_id, prompt content, or per-customer line items.
- Returning raw warehouse SQL or direct table access.
- Write actions (this is read-only).

High-level endpoint plan
- POST /console/api/internal/unit-economics/query
  - Single endpoint with a structured query body (preferred; easier for UI to evolve).
- (Optional) GET wrappers for common views can be added later.

AuthZ / gating
- Requires:
  - internal feature flag: unit_economics_dashboard_enabled
  - RBAC: role unit_econ_viewer (Finance + specific Eng/Product allowlist initially)
- Audit logging:
  - log caller, query dimensions, time_range, and row_count returned
  - do NOT log metric values in structured logs (sensitive)

Key concepts / vocabulary
- metric: what we compute
  - blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens
  - total_cost_usd
  - output_tokens
  - requests
  - avg_output_tokens_per_request
  - cache_hit_rate (if available per aggregation)
  - batching_efficiency (if available per aggregation)
- dimensions (group_by + filter keys)
  - time (implicit; controlled via granularity)
  - model_id (canonical internal model identifier)
  - model_version (serving version / snapshot)
  - quantization_profile (allowlisted short string)
  - region (canonical region)
  - customer_tier (self_serve | dedicated | private | enterprise)
  - streaming (true | false)
  - route (coarse route group; do not accept arbitrary route ids)

Granularity / bucketing
- granularity: hour | day | week
- constraints:
  - hour requires time_range <= 31d (soft limit; enforce if needed)
  - week only valid when time_range >= 28d (UI convenience)

Time range
- Use half-open intervals: [start, end)
- Timestamps in UTC in API; UI can display local, but query is UTC.

Query model (draft)
Request body (conceptual; not enforced yet):
{
  "view": "live" | "finance",
  "time_range": { "start": "2025-02-01T00:00:00Z", "end": "2025-02-08T00:00:00Z" },
  "granularity": "hour" | "day" | "week",
  "metric": "blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens",
  "group_by": ["region", "model_id"],
  "filters": {
    "region": ["us-east-1", "eu-west-1"],
    "customer_tier": ["self_serve", "enterprise"],
    "streaming": ["true"],
    "model_id": ["rw-llama-3-70b"],
    "quantization_profile": ["fp16", "int8"]
  },
  "order_by": { "field": "metric", "direction": "desc" },
  "limit": 50,
  "cursor": "...",
  "include_totals": true,
  "include_confidence": true
}

Notes
- filters values are lists; empty list == no filter.
- Some dimensions are only filterable, not groupable in v0 (e.g., route) depending on cardinality.
- “order_by.field” options:
  - metric (the computed metric selected)
  - output_tokens
  - total_cost_usd
  - requests

Response shape (draft)
{
  "meta": {
    "view": "live",
    "metric": "blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens",
    "unit": "usd_per_1m_output_tokens",
    "granularity": "hour",
    "time_range": {"start": "...", "end": "..."},
    "group_by": ["region", "model_id"],
    "next_cursor": "...",
    "row_count": 50,
    "generated_at": "2025-02-08T00:02:11Z",
    "data_freshness_lag_seconds": 420
  },
  "totals": {
    "total_cost_usd": 12345.67,
    "output_tokens": 987654321,
    "requests": 123456,
    "blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens": 12.50
  },
  "rows": [
    {
      "dim": {"region": "us-east-1", "model_id": "rw-llama-3-70b"},
      "series": [
        {
          "ts": "2025-02-01T00:00:00Z",
          "total_cost_usd": 120.12,
          "output_tokens": 11000000,
          "requests": 1400,
          "metric": 10.92,
          "confidence": "high",
          "coverage": "complete"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Implementation detail
- The response above is “rows each containing a series”.
- For pure time series without breakdowns (group_by empty), return a single row with dim {}.
- For “table breakdown without time series” (UI top-N tables), we can allow granularity = "all" OR series collapsed. Prefer explicit aggregation_mode field.

Proposed split: query_type / aggregation_mode
Option A (single endpoint with inferred behavior)
- If group_by is empty => return a single time series
- If group_by non-empty => return series per group
- UI can collapse series to last datapoint

Option B (explicit)
Request adds:
- "aggregation_mode": "timeseries" | "point_in_time" | "table"
- For "point_in_time", include "as_of": timestamp or derive from time_range.end - 1 bucket

Top-N support
We need an efficient way to ask:
- “Top 10 models by blended $/1M output tokens for last 7 days in eu-west-1, enterprise tier”

Top-N query (same endpoint; example)
{
  "view": "finance",
  "time_range": {"start": "2025-02-01T00:00:00Z", "end": "2025-02-08T00:00:00Z"},
  "granularity": "day",
  "metric": "blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens",
  "group_by": ["model_id"],
  "filters": {"region": ["eu-west-1"], "customer_tier": ["enterprise"]},
  "topn": {"n": 10, "by": "metric", "direction": "desc"},
  "aggregation_mode": "table"
}

Top-N response (table)
{
  "meta": {"...": "..."},
  "rows": [
    {
      "rank": 1,
      "dim": {"model_id": "rw-mistral-8x7b"},
      "total_cost_usd": 5200.00,
      "output_tokens": 200000000,
      "requests": 42000,
      "metric": 26.00,
      "confidence": "medium",
      "notes": "missing quantization_profile coverage for ~8% of rows"
    }
  ]
}

Pagination
- Cursor-based pagination for "table"/"breakdown" queries.
- cursor encodes stable ordering + last seen key.
- limit max: 500 (hard cap). Default: 50.

Validation / guardrails
- Dimension allowlist; reject unknown dimensions.
- High-cardinality protection:
  - quantization_profile must match allowlisted set (from model metadata registry)
  - route must be a stable coarse label (e.g., "chat_completions", "embeddings") not raw route id
  - model_version may be groupable only when filters.model_id is present (avoid exploding)
- Disallowed group_by combos (v0):
  - any group_by including customer_id or org_id (not supported)
  - group_by including both model_version and quantization_profile unless model_id filtered (TBD)

Confidence / coverage indicators (v0 idea)
- confidence: high | medium | low
- coverage: complete | partial | missing
- Computation sketch:
  - missing required dims (% rows with unknown region/tier/model) above threshold => confidence low
  - freshness lag above SLO => confidence medium/low
  - output_tokens == 0 with non-zero cost => confidence low (likely metering mismatch)

Errors
- 400 invalid_argument
  - invalid granularity
  - invalid time range (end <= start)
  - disallowed dimension / group_by
- 403 forbidden
  - user lacks unit_econ_viewer
- 404 not_found
  - feature flag disabled (or route not enabled)
- 429 too_many_requests
  - for abusive callers; internal UI should be safe with caching
- 503 unavailable
  - warehouse or materialized view refresh issue

Caching & freshness
- Two views (per Slack thread):
  - view=live: optimized for engineering debugging; lower TTL (e.g., 60s–120s), may show partial last hour
  - view=finance: optimized for KPI reporting; higher TTL (e.g., 15m), only returns completed buckets; stable rate card version pinned
- Response meta should include:
  - rate_card_version (string)
  - aggregation_job_watermark (timestamp)

Reconciliation endpoint (future)
- Potential separate endpoint for “dashboard totals vs billing totals” checks.
- Not needed for the UI MVP, but Finance will ask quickly.

Open questions / TODO
- Do we need compare_to support in v0 (previous period overlay)?
  - Could be client-side with 2 queries, but costs extra.
- Should we return both numerator/denominator and the computed metric always?
  - Strong preference yes; avoids rounding disputes.
- How to represent overhead + idle allocation in the API?
  - Option: expose cost_components breakdown as fields (compute_cost_usd, overhead_cost_usd, idle_cost_usd). Might be too detailed for v0; revisit.
- “model_id vs model_display_name”: UI wants friendly names; API should return canonical ids + optionally display_name field.

Changelog
- 2025-02-04: Added view=live vs view=finance concept + freshness metadata.
- 2025-02-12: Added aggregation_mode sketch; added guardrails around model_version grouping.
- 2025-02-18: Added confidence/coverage idea and notes field for partial coverage.
